newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks up in quiet trade ahead of CPI.
newsitem.headline: French stocks up in quiet trade ahead of CPI.

text.p: Paris stocks opened lower on Tuesday but quickly moved higher in early trade, helped by the dollar's strength against European currencies.

Brokers say the market will be calm ahead of U.S. economic data expected this afternoon, the consumer price index for May at 1230 GMT, and capacity utilisation and industrial production at 1315 GMT. The bourse is also seen treading water ahead of Prime Minister Lionel Jospin's policy speech on Thursday.
The CAC-40 index, which touched an all-time high on Monday of 2,825.18, was up 6.64 points, or 0.24 percent, at 2,802.51 at 0830 GMT. The CAC-40 futures contract was up seven at 2,792.
The markets rose on Monday on expectations EU leaders would bridge the differences between France and Germany on a pact to enforce budget discipline after the euro's launch in 1999.
Profit-taking emerged after a deal was struck including measures stressing jobs, sought by France, that were neither profligate nor likely to bring the jobless rate down fast.
* Consumer stocks continue to be seen as safe havens. Bic up 2.1 percent.

* Eurotunnel gives back some of Monday's gain, slipping 1.48 percent. Financial Times said creditor banks may seek to appoint another company to operate the Channel Tunnel link if shareholders do not approve the restructuring plan at the AGM on July 10.
